name: list_routines
description: List the workout routines saved in the user's openGym profile (the same list the Plan screen shows). Each routine is a named set of exercises with set/rep targets. Use this to discover the plan structure before diving into a specific routine or today's workout.

name: get_routine
description: Get the full exercise list for a single routine (the same view the routine editor shows). Returns mode (reps/time/cardio), set/rep/weight targets (a `pyramid` list of per-set rep targets, 'max' meaning as many reps as possible, when the exercise uses pyramid sets, with `pyramid_rest_sec` and `pyramid_weight` per set where planned, 0 meaning the exercise's rest or last time's weight), superset links, any per-exercise custom increment or Epley deload factor, and each exercise's own rest in seconds (absent means it inherits the global rest timer). Use routine_id from list_routines.

name: preview_session
description: Preview the session a routine will actually open with — the numbers the user will see after the progression policy and their training history have overridden the routine's own targets. This is NOT the same as get_routine: a routine storing "squat 3x8 @ 60kg" can open at 75kg because the policy progressed or deloaded from that routine's last logged session. The reps are the routine's own unless a policy that moves reps moved them, or the profile starts planned sessions from the last session (starts_from). Always call this (not get_routine) before telling someone what weight they are about to lift, or before judging whether an edit to a routine had any effect. Returns, per exercise, the planned target, the policy's decision and its stated reason, the opening set rows, and where each number came from. Defaults to today's scheduled routine.

routine_id.description: Routine to preview. Defaults to the routine scheduled for `date`.

date.description: Date the session would be started on, YYYY-MM-DD. Affects which routine is scheduled and any one-off day override. Defaults to today.

name: get_week_plan
description: Show the user's training plan. `days` is the authoritative answer to "what is planned when": the next seven dates from today with the routines planned for each (a date can hold several — a combined day) and how each was decided: a coach-week session ("coach"), a session the user pinned to that date ("pinned"), a one-off routine override ("override"), a "rest" override ("rest_override"), the weekday plan ("weekday") or nothing ("rest"). `coach_week` is the current coach week when one is running (a week written by an external planner through the API, never by the app): its sessions are done IN ORDER on whatever days the user trains (no weekday attached), the first undone one is today's session, a session can be pinned to a date, and `waiting` means the week starts on `starts_on`. `weekdays` is the user's own weekly plan keyed by JS getDay() (Sunday=0 … Saturday=6, the openGym state convention) — in a coach week it holds only the routines the user planned themselves, which ride along beside the coach-week session.

name: list_workouts
description: List recent finished workouts, newest first. Each item summarises the date, exercise count, sets done / planned, total volume (in the user's unit), duration and whether PRs were set. Use this before drilling into a specific date with get_workout.

from.description: Inclusive start date YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to no lower bound (list most recent).

to.description: Inclusive end date YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today.

limit.description: Max items to return. Defaults to 25.

name: get_workout
description: Get the full breakdown of one workout: every exercise, its mode (reps/time/cardio), the target, and per-set labels (e.g. "5 @ 60 kg", "1:30 · 20 kg"), and form_videos: how many sets the user filmed (a count only; the videos are never shared). Identify it by workout_id (from list_workouts) or by date. Use list_workouts first if you don't know either.

date.description: The workout date as YYYY-MM-DD. If two sessions share that date, the answer lists them instead and asks for a workout_id.

workout_id.description: The id from list_workouts. Preferred: it names one session even on a day with two.

name: estimate_1rm
description: Estimate one-rep max using Epley, Brzycki or Lombardi formulas. If an exercise_id is given, returns the all-time best estimate for that exercise with the source set (weight × reps + date) and the trend across history. If no exercise_id is given, returns a PR table across all reps-mode exercises (sorted highest first). Refuses to guess above 12 reps — above that, formulas diverge past 10% and "work capacity" is read instead of "maximal strength".

exercise_id.description: An exercise id from list_routines or get_workout entries. If omitted, returns a full PR table.

formula.description: Formula to use. Defaults to epley.

name: muscle_balance
description: Show which muscles the user has trained in a period, ranked by "effective sets" (volume in kg is intentionally not used — 100 kg leg press vs 12 kg lateral raise say nothing about which muscle worked harder). Reports worked muscles with a 0-4 relative level (1 = some work, 4 = most worked) and the muscles trained zero times in that period — useful for "what am I neglecting?" questions.

period.description: window: last 7 days, last 30 days, or all-time

name: get_programme
description: Show the user's programmes: routines run as a block of 1 to 16 calendar weeks, each week with optional targets (a %1RM per exercise, an RPE per exercise or for the whole week, a deload week). `running` is the one in progress, or null: its current week (1-based) of how many, whether it is paused or done, and this week's targets. While one runs, its schedule IS the user's weekday plan or rotation (get_week_plan shows it), and preview_session already opens sessions at its targets. `programmes` lists every saved one with its schedule and weeks. Targets are keyed by exercise id, or by "routineId:exerciseId" for one routine only.

name: search_exercises
description: Search openGym's exercise library (the built-in catalogue plus the user's own exercises) by name, muscle or equipment, e.g. "romanian deadlift", "rear delt dumbbell", "pull-up bar". Returns ids with name, body part, target muscle, equipment and category, best match first. Use it before create_routine, update_routine or log_workout whenever a name could mean several exercises (there are many curls and presses): pass the id you picked as `exercise`, and the save cannot land on the wrong one. Filter with body_part, equipment (as the results spell it: "barbell", "dumbbell", "body weight", "cable", "leverage machine", "band"...) or category to build a plan from what the user owns.

query.description: Words to look for. Omit to list by the filters alone.

limit.description: How many to return, 15 by default.

name: log_workout
description: Log a workout the user describes into their openGym history (it syncs to all their devices). Turn what they said into exercises and one entry per set: "curls, 12 kg, 12/12/10" is three sets of {reps, weight: 12}; "3 sets of 12, except the last was 10" is 12, 12, 10. Ask instead of assuming when the weight, the number of sets or the reps are unclear. Exercises are matched against the user's library by name or id. A common name resolves to the library's default variant ("shoulder press" is the barbell one): when the reply's `name` differs from `you_said` and the variant matters (dumbbell vs barbell, machine vs cable), confirm with the user, or pass an id. If a name matches several exercises, or none, nothing is saved and `problems` lists candidates: ask the user which one, then call again with its id. Only set create_custom for an exercise the user confirms is not in the library. Call with dry_run: true first when you had to interpret anything, show the user the preview, and log it once they agree. Cardio is minutes per set plus speed or distance and an optional incline: "20 min treadmill walk at 3.5 mph, incline 7" is {exercise: "treadmill", sets: [{minutes: 20, speed: 3.5, incline: 7}]} with speed_unit "mph". Calling again with the same description does not log it twice. Supersets are not supported here.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD the session was done; defaults to today. Not in the future.

start.description: Start time HH:MM, if the user said it. Without it a session logged today ends now; one in the past starts at 18:00.

duration_min.description: How long the session took, in minutes, if known.

name.description: A name for the session, e.g. "Arms" or "Push day". Defaults to "Workout".

note.description: A note on the whole session.

unit.description: The unit the user gave weights in; defaults to the profile's. Converted when it differs.

speed_unit.description: The unit cardio speeds (and distances: km or mi) are given in; defaults to the profile's.

exercise.description: Exercise name as the user said it ("dumbbell curl"), or an exercise id from search_exercises or an earlier answer.

create_custom.description: Create this as the user's own exercise when the library has nothing matching. Only after the user confirms.

body_part.description: Body part of a new custom exercise, when its name does not say.

note.description: A note on this exercise today.

reps.description: Reps done. Give reps for a rep exercise, or seconds for a hold, never both in one exercise.

seconds.description: Seconds held, for a timed exercise (plank, hang, wall sit).

weight.description: Load in `unit`. Omit or 0 for bodyweight. On an assistance machine it is the help (less is better). For dumbbells: as the profile logs that exercise (see weight_means in the reply).

warmup.description: A warm-up set: kept out of volume, PRs and the next suggested weight.

rir.description: Reps in reserve, if the user said it. Not with rpe.

rpe.description: RPE, if the user said it. Not with rir. The only effort a cardio set takes.

minutes.description: Cardio only (treadmill, bike, rower…): whole minutes of this interval. A cardio set is minutes plus speed or distance, never reps or weight.

speed.description: Cardio: average speed in speed_unit. Omit when nobody said it.

distance.description: Cardio: distance covered, km (or miles with speed_unit mph), instead of the speed. Not with speed.

incline.description: Cardio on foot (treadmill, stairs): grade in percent. Refused on a bike or rower.

dry_run.description: Build and return the preview without saving anything.

allow_duplicate.description: Log it even though the same sets are already logged that day (a genuine second session). Give it a different start or name too.

name: create_routine
description: Create a routine in the user's openGym plan (it syncs to all their devices), e.g. "squat 5 × 5 at 100 kg, plank 3 × 60 s, Tuesdays and Fridays". Exercises are matched against the library like log_workout: when a name matches several or none, nothing is saved and `problems` lists candidates to put to the user. Each exercise starts the way picking it in the app starts it; only what you pass is set on top. `weekdays` puts it on those days of the weekly plan, next to whatever is planned there already. Call with dry_run: true first when you interpreted anything, show the preview, and save once the user agrees.

exercise.description: Exercise name as the user said it ("barbell squat"), or an exercise id from search_exercises or an earlier answer (an id never matches the wrong exercise).

sets.description: Number of sets. Omit for the profile's default (3 unless they set their own).

reps.description: Reps per set, for a rep exercise.

seconds.description: Seconds per set, for a hold (plank). Not with reps.

weight.description: Planned load in `unit`; omit or 0 to start from what the user lifted last time.

rest_sec.description: Rest after each set, seconds. 0 or omitted: the global rest timer.

note.description: A note shown with this exercise in the workout.

weekdays.description: The weekdays to plan it on.

unit.description: The unit weights are given in; defaults to the profile's.

name: update_routine
description: Change a routine: rename it, replace its exercise list, append exercises, or move it to other weekdays. Use routine_id from list_routines. `exercises` is the whole new list in order; an exercise named again keeps everything its slot had (rest, warm-ups, progression, notes) except what you pass. `add_exercises` appends. `weekdays` is every day it should be on (it leaves the others); omit it to leave the schedule alone. Pass expected_revision (from get_routine) when the user confirmed a change against what they saw: if the profile moved since, nothing is saved and you get a conflict to read again.

exercise.description: Exercise name as the user said it ("barbell squat"), or an exercise id from search_exercises or an earlier answer (an id never matches the wrong exercise).

sets.description: Number of sets. Omit for the profile's default (3 unless they set their own).

reps.description: Reps per set, for a rep exercise.

seconds.description: Seconds per set, for a hold (plank). Not with reps.

weight.description: Planned load in `unit`; omit or 0 to start from what the user lifted last time.

rest_sec.description: Rest after each set, seconds. 0 or omitted: the global rest timer.

note.description: A note shown with this exercise in the workout.

exercise.description: Exercise name as the user said it ("barbell squat"), or an exercise id from search_exercises or an earlier answer (an id never matches the wrong exercise).

sets.description: Number of sets. Omit for the profile's default (3 unless they set their own).

reps.description: Reps per set, for a rep exercise.

seconds.description: Seconds per set, for a hold (plank). Not with reps.

weight.description: Planned load in `unit`; omit or 0 to start from what the user lifted last time.

rest_sec.description: Rest after each set, seconds. 0 or omitted: the global rest timer.

note.description: A note shown with this exercise in the workout.

name: delete_routine
description: Delete a routine from the plan, and from every weekday and date it was planned on. Logged workouts stay. Only after the user said yes to deleting that routine by name: pass confirm: true and expected_revision from get_routine or list_routines. If the profile changed since, nothing is deleted and you get a conflict to read again.

confirm.description: The user agreed to delete this routine.
